About

Between art and psychoanalytic thinking

I am Akrivi (Vivi) Kopanitsanou, a certified Art Psychotherapist (ECP-h) and Mental Health Counsellor with an M.Sc. in Child Development Psychology. At my practice at 42 Al. Papanastasiou in Neo Psychiko, close to Panormou metro station, I work with children, adolescents and adults, individually and in groups.

I studied Education at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens, completed an M.Sc. in Psychology of Child Development (UCLan) and trained in Art Psychotherapy for Children and Adults at the Art and Psychotherapy Centre (2013 – 2019).

During my clinical training I gained experience in mental-health and child-protection services — the Day Centre of the Byron Families' Association for Mental Health (S.O.P.Y.), the «Agios Andreas» children's community and the Child Guidance Service of EKEPSYE Piraeus — working therapeutically with children who had experienced abuse, adults with severe mental-health difficulties, and children with emotional difficulties and eating-related issues.

Today I coordinate and teach on the M.Sc. in Art Psychotherapy for Children and Adults at ICPS – College of Humanistic Sciences, in collaboration with the University of Lancashire, and I am a collaborating member of the psychoanalytic practice EPEKEINA.

I believe in continuous professional development, in clinical supervision and in the value of research in psychotherapeutic practice.

Vivi Kopanitsanou

The approach

Art Psychotherapy, with psychoanalytic thinking

An in-depth psychotherapeutic approach: words and the creative process work at the same time as means of expression, understanding and working through psychic experience. No artistic knowledge or skills are needed.

Inspired by the two paintings in her studio — the wave and the calm.

  1. 01

    Expression

    In words, with a line, with a colour — whatever finds its way first. On paper, what is hard to say can take shape.

  2. 02

    Understanding

    The image and the words become a starting point to understand together what troubles you, and the way you relate to others.

  3. 03

    Working through

    Within a stable frame of safety, consistency and trust, experience is worked through in depth, at your own pace.

The therapeutic relationship

A stable frame, at the heart of the work

At the centre of my work is the therapeutic relationship and the creation of a stable frame, within which you can explore in depth what troubles you and understand yourself better.

I

Safety

A space where you can express yourself freely, without judgement.

II

Consistency

The same place and a steady presence, session after session.

III

Trust

So that you can look in depth at what weighs on you, and at the way you relate to others.

Sessions & groups

For children, adolescents and adults

Individual sessions last 60 minutes and take place at the practice in Neo Psychiko. Groups and workshops run on their own schedule — ask about the next one.

Booking

Do I need to know how to draw?

No. Art Psychotherapy does not require any artistic knowledge or skills; art materials are simply another means of expression, alongside words.

Who do you work with?

Children, adolescents and adults, in individual sessions and in groups. I also meet parents, individually or in parent groups.

How long is a session?

60 minutes for an individual session. Parent groups and personal-development groups last 120 minutes, and experiential group workshops 180 minutes.

Where is the practice?

At 42 Al. Papanastasiou, Neo Psychiko (154 51), about 600 metres from Panormou metro station. The «Vouri» and «Lito» bus stops are close by.

How do I book an appointment?

By phone on 694 769 3984, or online on doctoranytime, where the available times are shown.

How do I pay?

At the practice, by card or in cash.

Can I cancel an appointment?

Yes, up to 24 hours before the session.

What does ECP mean?

It is the European Certificate of Psychotherapy of the European Association for Psychotherapy (EAP), of which I am a member.
